In the place of the Lord of the Kulikas, there is Vajraḍākinī. Therefore, by virtue of their respective positions, she who is Vajraḍākinī becomes the Kulikā,
and she who is Vajravārāhī becomes Vajraḍākinī.

Then, at the morning twilight, with the rising of the southern face, there is a movement of Vajraḍākinī, the Kulikā, from the central position of the presiding deity to the southern petal; and Lāmā moves from the central position of the presiding deity [to the north]. Thus, by virtue of their positions, she who was Vajraḍākinī, the Kulikā, becomes Lāmā.
She who is Lāmā becomes the Kulikā.
Then, at the junction of midday, with the rising of the western face, there is the movement of Lāmā-Kulikā from her position as the presiding deity in the center to the western petal,
and the movement of Khaṇḍarohā to the central position of the presiding deity.
Then, by virtue of the position, she who is the *lāmā* of the *kulikā* becomes *khaṇḍarohā*;
she who is *khaṇḍarohā* becomes the *kulikā*.
Thereafter, at the evening twilight (*aparāhṇa-saṃdhyā*) during the rising of the northern face, there is the movement of *khaṇḍarohā-kulikā* upon the northern petal.
In the center of Rūpiṇī is the position of the sovereign. Then, by virtue of that position, she who is Khaṇḍarohā, the Kulikā, becomes Rūpiṇī;
and she who is Rūpiṇī becomes the Kulikā.
On the second day, on the second lunar date (*dvitīyā*), there is the movement of Rūpiṇī, Kulikā, and the others.
There, at the juncture of midnight, with the rising of the eastern face, Rūpiṇī, as Kulikā, moves from her position as the central sovereign to the eastern petal;
Vajravārāhī, as Ḍākinī, occupies the central sovereign position.
Then, by virtue of her position, she becomes the embodied Vajraḍākinī;
Vajravārāhīḍākinī becomes the Kulikā.
Then, at the morning twilight—
The movement of Vajravārāhī, the Kulikā, is on the southern petal;
that of Vajraḍākinī Lāmā is in the center, the position of the sovereign.
Consequently, by virtue of their positions, Vajravārāhī becomes Lāmā.
Vajraḍākinī, who is Lāmā, becomes the Kulikā. Therefore, at the midday junction, Vajraḍākinī-Lāmā-Kulikā moves to the western petal,
while Lāmā-Khaṇḍarohā remains in the center, the position of the sovereign.
Then, by virtue of their respective positions, she who is Vajraḍākinī, the Kulikā Lāmā, becomes Khaṇḍarohā;
and she who is Lāmā, Khaṇḍarohā, becomes the Kulikā.
Consequently, at the evening twilight of the afternoon, there is the movement of the Kulikā Lāmā-Khaṇḍarohā upon the northern petal.
Khaṇḍarohā-Rūpiṇī is in the center, in the position of the sovereign.
Then, by virtue of their respective positions, she who is Lāmā-Khaṇḍarohā, the Kulikā, becomes Rūpiṇī;
and she who was Khaṇḍarohā-Rūpiṇī becomes the Kulikā.
Third Day: Then, on the third day, during the third [watch], there is the movement of Khaṇḍarohā, Kulikā, and the others.
There, at the juncture of midnight, with the rising of the eastern face, there is the movement of Khaṇḍarohā in the form of Kulikā upon the eastern petal;
and of Rūpiṇī-Vajraḍākinī in the center, in the place of the sovereign.
Then, by virtue of their respective positions, she who is the *Kulikā* in the form of Khaṇḍarohā becomes Vajraḍākinī;
and she who is Rūpiṇīvajraḍākinī becomes the *Kulikā*.
Thereafter, at the morning twilight, with the arising of the southern face, there is the movement of Rūpiṇīvajraḍākinī, the *Kulikā*, onto the southern petal.
Vajravārāhī and Lāmā are in the central position as the presiding deities. Then, by virtue of their respective positions, she who is Rūpiṇī and belongs to the Vajraḍākinī family becomes Lāmā;
and she who is Vajravārāhī and Lāmā becomes the Kulikā.
Then, at the midday junction during the rising of the western face, there is the movement of Vajravārāhī Lāmākulikā to the western petal;
Vajraḍākinī Khaṇḍarohā is in the center, in the position of the sovereign.
Consequently, by virtue of their respective positions, Vajravārāhī becomes Lāmākulikā and Khaṇḍarohā.
Vajraḍākinī Khaṇḍarohā becomes the Kulikā.
Then, at the evening twilight of the afternoon, with the rising of the northern face, there is the movement of Vajraḍākinī Khaṇḍarohā-Kulikā to the northern petal,
while Lāmā Rūpiṇī occupies the central position as the presiding deity.
Then, by virtue of the positions, she who is Vajraḍākinī-Khaṇḍarohā becomes Rūpiṇī;
she who is Lāmā-Rūpiṇī becomes Kulikā.
On the fourth day, on the fourth lunar day, there is the movement of Lāmā-Kulikā and the others.
There, at the junction of midnight, when the eastern face rises, there is the movement of Lāmārūpiṇī Kulikā upon the eastern petal;
Khaṇḍarohā-Vajraḍākinī is in the center, in the position of the sovereign.
Thus, by virtue of the [respective] positions.
Lāmārūpiṇī is the Kulikā Vajraḍākinī;
Khaṇḍarohā is the Kulikā Vajraḍākinī.
Then, at the morning twilight, with the arising of the southern face, there is the movement of Khaṇḍarohā, the Kulikā Vajraḍākinī, upon the southern petal.
Rūpiṇīlāmā is in the center, in the position of the sovereign.
Then, by virtue of that position, Khaṇḍarohāvajraḍākinī becomes Kulikā Lāmā, and Rūpiṇīlāmā becomes Kulikā.
Therefore, at the junction of midday, with the rising of the western face, there is the movement of Rūpiṇīlāmā Kulikā onto the western petal.

Vajravārāhī and Khaṇḍarohā are in the center, in the place of the sovereign. Then, by virtue of their positions, she who is Rūpiṇī and the Kulikā Lāmā becomes Khaṇḍarohā; and she who is Vajravārāhī and Khaṇḍarohā becomes the Kulikā.
Then, at the evening twilight during the rising of the northern face, Vajravārāhī-Khaṇḍarohākulikā moves to the northern petal;
Vajraḍākinīrūpiṇī occupies the central position as the presiding deity.
Consequently, by virtue of this shift in positions, Vajravārāhī-Khaṇḍarohākulikā [occupies the center].
She who possesses form—
she who has the form of Vajraḍākinī— is the Kulikā. On the fifth day, on the fifth lunar date, there is the movement of Vajraḍākinī, Kulikā, and the others.
There, at the twilight of midnight during the rising of the eastern face, there is the movement of Vajraḍākinī in the form of Kulikā upon the eastern petal;
Lāmā-Vajraḍākinī is in the center, in the position of the sovereign.

Then, by virtue of the position, that Vajraḍākinī becomes the lineage-holder (kulikā) Lāmā in the form of Khaṇḍarohā; she returns once again to her own place as Vajraḍākinī during the first full moon.

Then, at the eastern twilight, with the arising of the southern face, there is the movement of Lāmā-Vajraḍākinī, the lineage-holder, onto the southern petal, while Khaṇḍarohā-Lāmā moves to the center.
Then, by virtue of the [changing] positions, that Lāmā who has the form of Khaṇḍarohā becomes Vajraḍākinī Kulikā; having been so, she returns once again to her own place as Lāmā.
That Khaṇḍarohā-Lāmā becomes the Kulikā.
Then, at the midday junction, with the rising of the western face, there is the movement of Khaṇḍarohā-Lāmā-Kulikā onto the western petal.
In the center is Rūpiṇī-Khaṇḍarohā.
Then, by virtue of their respective positions, that Khaṇḍarohā becomes Rūpiṇī-Vajraḍākinī-Lāmā-Kulikā, and returning to her own place, she once again becomes Khaṇḍarohā.
That Rūpiṇī-Khaṇḍarohā becomes the Kulikā.
Then, at the following twilight, with the rising of the northern face, there is the movement of Rūpiṇī Khaṇḍarohā Kulikā on the northern petal;
Vajravārāhī Rūpiṇī is in the center.
Then, by virtue of the shift in position, she who was Rūpiṇī becomes Vajraḍākinī, Lāmā, and Khaṇḍarohā—the Kulikā—and returns once again to her own place as Rūpiṇī.
She who was Vajravārāhī-Rūpiṇī becomes Vajraḍākinī, Lāmā, and Khaṇḍarohā—those who are not Rūpiṇī—and returns once again to her own place as the Kulikā.
Thus, on the fifth day, during the twenty twilights, this movement occurs through the transition into the twenty aspects of perfect awakening.

[The deities] Vajravārāhī and the others—Nandā, Bhadrā, Jayā, Riktā, and Pūrṇā—correspond respectively to the lunar days (tithis) of the first, second, third, fourth, and fifth; by way of their nature as the five lunar digits (candrakalā), they constitute the division of the first bliss (*prathamānanda*).
Thus, as it is on the first day, so it is on the sixth.
As it is on the second day, so it is on the seventh;
as it is on the third, so it is on the eighth;
as it is on the fourth, so it is on the ninth.
Just as on the fifth day, so on the tenth day there is a transition by means of the division of supreme bliss (*paramānanda*). Likewise, as on the sixth day, so on the eleventh day;
as on the seventh day, so on the twelfth day.
As on the eighth day, so on the thirteenth;
as on the ninth, so on the fourteenth;
as on the tenth, so on the full moon—thus the movement occurs through the distinction of the bliss of cessation (*viramānanda*).
At the end of that, having performed the great worship (mahāpūjā), there is the movement of the four yoginīs during the first fortnight.

The Mahāśmaśānasaṃcāra: On the first day of the second dark fortnight, during the first watch from midnight, there is a movement (*saṃcāra*) in the eastern great cremation ground (*mahāśmaśāna*) of Kulikā, and in the center, at the place of the sovereign (*adhipati*), is Kākāsyā.
Consequently, by virtue of that location, [the goddess] is Kulikā.
Kākāsyā becomes Kākāsyā when she is the Kulikā;
thereafter, in the second watch, there is the movement of Kākāsyā and Kulikā in the great southern cremation ground,
and that of Ulūkāsyā in the center.
Then, by virtue of the location, Kākāsyā becomes the Kulikā Ulūkāsyā;
Ulūkāsyā becomes the Kulikā.
Then, in the third watch, the movement of Ulūkāsyā-Kulikā takes place in the western great cremation ground.
In the center is Śvānāsyā. Then, by virtue of their positions, Ulūkāsyā becomes the Kulikā of Śvānāsyā,
and Śvānāsyā becomes the Kulikā.
Then, during the fourth watch, there is the movement of Śvānāsyākulikā in the northern great cremation ground,
and that of Śūkarāsyā in the center.
Consequently, by virtue of the location, Śvānāsyākulikā becomes Śūkarāsyā.
Śūkarāsyā becomes the Kulikā;
thus, by the rightward rotation of the earring, there is a movement on the solar side through the division of the four watches.
Then, from midday, during the first watch in the lunar portion, there is the movement of the lineage-holder Śūkarāsyā in the great cremation ground in the northeast;
Yamadāḍhī is in the center.
Consequently, by virtue of the location, Śūkarāsyā becomes Yamadāḍhī.
Yamadāḍhī becomes the Kulikā.
Then, in the second watch, there is the movement of Yamadāḍhī, the Kulikā, in the Vāyavya great cremation ground;
[the movement] of Yamadūtī is in the center.
Then, by virtue of the position, Yamadāḍhī becomes the Kulikā Yamadūtī;
she who is Yamadūtī becomes the Kulikā.
Thereafter, in the third watch, the movement of the Kulikā Yamadūtī occurs in the great cremation ground of Nairṛtya.
Yamadaṃṣṭriṇī is in the center.
Then, by virtue of their positions, Yamadūtī becomes Kulikā Yamadaṃṣṭriṇī;
she who was Yamadaṃṣṭriṇī becomes Kulikā.

Then, during the fourth watch, there is the movement of the *kulikā* Yamadaṃṣṭriṇī in the great cremation ground of Agni, and that of Yamamathanī in the center. Consequently, by virtue of their respective locations, the *kulikā* Yamadaṃṣṭriṇī becomes Yamamathanī.
She who is Yamamathanī becomes Kulikā;
thus, by the counter-clockwise rotation of the earring, the movement of the Yoginīs occurs in the lunar portion.
In this manner, the movement of the Yoginīs on the first day is to be understood.
On the second day, during the first watch from midnight, there is the movement of Yamamathanī Kulikā in the eastern great cremation ground;
Vajravārāhī Kākāsyā is in the center. Then, by virtue of the location, Yamamathanī Kulikā becomes Kākāsyā.
She who is Vajravārāhī-Kākāsyā is the Kulikā.
Therefore, during the second watch, there is the movement of the Kulikā Vajravārāhī to the southern great cremation ground,
between Kākāsyā and Ulūkāsyā.
Then, by virtue of the [respective] positions, Ulūkāsyā becomes the *Kulikā* of the Vajravārāhī family;
she who was Kākāsyā-Ulūkāsyā becomes the *Kulikā*.
Thereafter, during the third watch, there is the movement of Kākāsyā, the *Kulikā*, in the great charnel ground of the West.
Between Ulūkāsyā and Śvānāsyā,
then by virtue of their positions, Kākāsyā becomes Śvānāsyā;
she who was Ulūkāsyā becomes Śvānāsyā, and she [the former Śvānāsyā] becomes Kulikā.
Then, during the fourth watch, the lineage goddess Ulūkāsyā moves about in the northern great cremation ground;
Śvānāsyā and Sūkarāsyā are in the center.
Then, by virtue of their respective locations, Ulūkāsyā and Sūkarāsyā—(40)
She who has the face of a dog or the face of a pig is the Kulikā;
thus is the movement by way of the right-turning of the earring in the solar portion.
Then, during the first watch after midday, when the moon is in its waning phase, there is the movement of Śvānāsyā and Kulikā in the Īśāna Mahāśmaśāna;
Śūkarāsyā and Yamadāḍhī are in the center. Subsequently, according to their respective positions, Śvānāsyā becomes Kulikā and Yamadāḍhī [becomes Śūkarāsyā].

She who is Śūkarāsyā is Yamadāḍhī; she becomes the Kulikā. Then, in the second watch, there is the movement of Śūkarāsyā, the Kulikā, in the great cremation ground of Vāyavya, and of Yamadāḍhī, who is Yamadūtī, in the center.
Then, by virtue of the position, the lineage-holder Śūkarāsyā becomes Yamadūtī;
she who is Yamadāḍhī-Yamadūtī becomes the lineage-holder.
Then, in the third watch, the lineage-holder Yamadāḍhī moves about in the great charnel ground of Nairṛtya.
In the center is Yamadūtī-Yamadaṃṣṭriṇī.
Then, by virtue of their positions, Yamadāḍhī becomes Kulikā Yamadaṃṣṭriṇī;
she who was Yamadūtī-Yamadaṃṣṭriṇī becomes Kulikā.
Then, during the fourth watch, there is the movement of Yamadūtī Kulikā in the great cremation ground of Agneya;
[she is] between Yamadaṃṣṭriṇī and Yamamathanī.
Consequently, by virtue of her position, Yamadūtī Kulikā becomes Yamamathanī.
She who is Yamadaṃṣṭriṇī is Amathanī; she becomes the Kulikā.
Thus, by the counter-clockwise rotation of the earring, the movement of the Yoginīs occurs within the lunar portion.
On the third day, then, at the first watch after midnight, there is the movement of Yamadaṃṣṭriṇī-Kulikā in the great cremation ground to the east.
Between Yamamathani and Kākāsyā is [the goddess] Yamadaṃṣṭriṇī; by virtue of her position, she becomes the Kulikā Kākāsyā. She who is Yamamathani-Kākāsyā becomes the Kulikā.

Then, during the second watch, there is the movement of Yamamathanī Kulikā in the southern great cremation ground; [the movement] of Vajravārāhī Ulūkāsyā is in the center. Consequently, by virtue of the location, Yamamathanī becomes Ulūkāsyā.
Vajravārāhī-Ulūkāsyā is the Kulikā;
therefore, during the third watch, there is the movement of Vajravārāhī, the Kulikā, in the western great cremation ground.
Between Kākāsyā and Śvānāsyā;
therefore, by virtue of their positions, Śvānāsyā becomes the Kulikā of Vajravārāhī.
She who is Kākāsyā and Śvānāsyā is the Kulikā.
Then, during the fourth watch, there is the movement of Kākāsyā Kulikā in the northern great cemetery;
that of Ulūkāsyā and Śūkarāsyā is in the center.
Consequently, due to the influence of the location, Kākāsyā Kulikā becomes Śūkarāsyā.
She who is Ulūkāsyā is Kulikā when she is Śūkarāsyā;
thus is the movement by the clockwise rotation of the earring on the solar side.
Then, on the lunar side, during the first watch before midday, there is the movement of Ulūkāsyā-Kulikā in the great cemetery of Īśāna.
Śvānāsyā is in the center of Yamadāḍhī;
then, by virtue of their positions, Ulūkāsyā becomes Kulikā and Yamadāḍhī [becomes Śvānāsyā].
She who is Śvānāsyā (Dog-faced) and Yamadāḍhī (Fierce-toothed Yama) becomes the Kulikā.
Then, in the second watch, there is the movement of the Kulikā Śvānāsyā in the great cremation ground of Vāyavya (the northwest),
and of Śūkarāsyā (Pig-faced) Yamadūtī in the center.
Then, by virtue of their positions, Śavāsyā becomes Yamadūtī and Kulikā; and she who was Yamadūtī and Śūkarāsyā becomes Kulikā.
Thereafter, during the third watch, there is the movement of Śūkarāsyā, the Kulikā, in the great cremation ground of Nairṛtya.
Between Yamadāḍhī and Yamadaṃṣṭriṇī,
then, by virtue of their positions, Śūkarāsyā becomes Yamadaṃṣṭriṇī,
and Yamadāḍhī— who was Yamadaṃṣṭriṇī— becomes Kulikā.
Then, during the fourth watch, there is the movement of Yamadāḍhī Kulikā in the great cremation ground of Āgneya;
she is in the center between Yamadūtī and Yamamathanī.
Consequently, by virtue of her position, Yamadāḍhī Kulikā becomes Yamamathanī.
She who is Yamadūtī, the Destroyer of Yama, she becomes the Kulikā.
Thus is the movement by the counter-clockwise rotation of the earring.
On the fourth day, from the Kulikā, Yamadūtī moves in the first watch after midnight in the great cremation ground of the East.
Between Yamadaṃṣṭriṇī and Kākāsyā is Mandhyā.
Then, by virtue of their positions, Yamadūtī becomes Kākāsyā Kulikā;
that which was Yamadaṃṣṭriṇī-Kākāsyā becomes the Kulikā.

Then, during the second watch, there is the movement of Yamadaṃṣṭriṇī Kulikā in the southern great cremation ground; [and] of Yamamathanī Ulūkāsyā in the center. Consequently, due to the influence of the positions, Yamadaṃṣṭriṇī becomes Ulūkāsyā Kulikā;
and she who is Yamamathanī Ulūkāsyā becomes Kulikā.
Then, during the third watch, there is the movement of Yamamathanī Kulikā in the western great cremation ground;
Vajravārāhī Śvānāsyā is in the center.
Consequently, by virtue of the location, Yamamathanī Kulikā becomes Śvānāsyā.
She who is Vajravārāhī-Śvānāsyā becomes the Kulikā.
Therefore, during the fourth watch, there is the movement of the Kulikā Vajravārāhī in the northern great cremation ground,
and that of Kākāsyā and Śūkarāsyā in the center.
Then, by virtue of the position, Vajravārāhī becomes the Kulikā Śūkarāsyā (Boar-faced).
She who was Kākāsyā becomes the Kulikā Śūkarāsyā.
Thus, by the clockwise rotation of the Kundalī, there is a movement within the solar portion.
Then, during the first watch after midday within the lunar portion, there is the movement of Kākāsyā Kulikā in the great charnel ground of Īśāna;
Ulūkāsyā Yamadāḍhī is in the center.
Consequently, by virtue of their positions, Kākāsyā Kulikā becomes Yamadāḍhī.

Ulūkāsyā is the *āḍhī*; she is the *kulikā*. Then, in the second watch, there is the movement of Ulūkāsyā, the *kulikā*, in the great charnel ground of Vāyavya, and of Śvānāsyā, the Yama-messenger, in the center.
Then, by virtue of her position, Ulūkāsyā becomes Yamadūtī the Kulikā; she who was Śvānāsyā Yamadūtī becomes the Kulikā.
In the third watch, [this occurs] for Śvānāsyā the Kulikā.
There is a movement in the great charnel ground of Nairṛtya.
Śūkarāsyā Yamadaṃṣṭriṇī is in the center; then, by virtue of her position, Śvānāsyā becomes Kulikā Yamadaṃṣṭriṇī. She who was Śūkarāsyā Yamadaṃṣṭriṇī becomes the Kulikā.
Then, during the fourth watch, there is the movement of the sow-faced Kaulikā in the great cremation ground of Agni;
Yamadāḍhī and Yamamathanī are in the center.
Consequently, by virtue of their positions, the sow-faced Kaulikā becomes Yamamathanī.
Yamadāḍhī and Yamamathanī—she who is [the latter] becomes the Kulikā.
Thus, by the counter-clockwise rotation of the Kundalinī, the movement of the Yoginīs occurs within the lunar portion.
On the fifth day, during the first watch from midnight, the movement of Yamadāḍhī, the Kulikā, takes place in the eastern cremation ground.
In the center is Kākāsyā, who is Yamadūtī;
then, by virtue of her position, Yamadāḍhī becomes Kākāsyā. She who was Yamadūtī-Kākāsyā becomes the Kulikā.
Then, during the second watch, there is the movement of Yamadūtī Kulikā in the southern great cremation ground;
[the movement] of Yamadaṃṣṭriṇī Ulūkāsyā is in the center.
Consequently, by virtue of the location, Yamadūtī Kulikā becomes Ulūkāsyā.
Yamadaṃṣṭriṇī, who has the face of an owl, is the Kulikā.
Then, during the third watch, there is the movement of Yamadaṃṣṭriṇī, the Kulikā, in the western great cremation ground;
[the movement] of Yamamathanī and Śvānāsyā is in the center.
Then, by virtue of the position, Yamadaṃṣṭriṇī becomes Kulikā Śvānāsyā;
that which was Yamamathanī Śvānāsyā becomes Kulikā.
Consequently, in the fourth watch, there is the movement of Yamamathanī Kulikā in the northern Mahāśmaśāna.
In the center is Vajravārāhī Śūkarāsyā. Then, by virtue of her position, Yamamathanī becomes the Kulikā Śūkarāsyā;
she who is Vajravārāhī Śūkarāsyā is the Kulikā.
Thus, by means of the clockwise rotation starting from Kuṇḍalā, is the movement of the Yoginīs during the solar portion.
Then, during the lunar portion, from midday through the first watch, there is the movement of Vajravārāhī, the Kulikā, in the great cremation ground of Īśāna;
and that of Kākāsyā, the fierce Yamadāḍhī, in the center.
Then, by virtue of her position, Yamadāḍhī becomes the Kulikā of the Vajravārāhī family;
she who is Kākāsyā-Yamadāḍhī is the Kulikā.
Subsequently, in the second watch, there is the movement of the Kulikā Kākāsyā in the great cremation ground of the northwest.
Ulūkāsyā is in the middle of the Yama-messenger;
then, by virtue of her position, Kākāsyā becomes the Kulikā-Yama-messenger,
and she who was Ulūkāsyā-Yama-messenger becomes the Kulikā.
Then, during the third watch, there is the movement of Ulūkāsyā Kulikā in the great charnel ground of Nairṛtya,
and of Śvānāsyā Yamadaṃṣṭriṇī in the center.
Consequently, due to the shifting of positions, Yamadaṃṣṭriṇī becomes [the occupant] of the place of Ulūkāsyā Kulikā.
She who is Dog-faced (Śvānāsyā) and has fangs is the Kulikā.
Therefore, during the fourth watch, there is the movement of the Kulikā Śvānāsyā in the great cremation ground of Agni,
and that of Sūkarāsyā and Yamamathanī in the center.
Then, by virtue of their positions, Śvānāsyā becomes Yamamathanī the Kulikā;
and she who was Śūkarāsyā-Yamamathanī becomes the Kulikā.
Thus, by the counter-clockwise rotation of the earring, the movement of the Yoginīs occurs within the lunar portion.
(43) On the sixth day, during the first watch from midnight, there is the movement of the sow-faced Kulikā in the eastern great cremation ground;
that of Yamadāḍhī, the crow-faced one, is in the center.
Consequently, by virtue of the location, the sow-faced Kulikā becomes the crow-faced one.
She who is Yamadāḍhīkākāsyā is the Kulikā.
Then, during the second watch, there is the movement of Yamadāḍhī, the Kulikā, in the great southern cremation ground;
[the movement] of Yamadūtī and Ulūkāsyā is in the center.
Then, by virtue of the position, Yamadāḍhī becomes Ulūkāsyā Kulikā;
that which is Yamadūtī-Ulūkāsyā becomes the Kulikā.
Then, in the third watch, there is the movement of Yamadūtī Kulikā in the western great cremation ground.
Between Yamadaṃṣṭriṇī and Śvānāsyā is Kulikā;
thus, by virtue of their positions, Yamadūtī becomes Śvānāsyā,
and she who was Yamadaṃṣṭriṇī becomes Kulikā.
Then, during the fourth watch, there is the movement of Yamadaṃṣṭriṇī, the Kulikā, in the northern great cremation ground;
[the movement] of Yamamathanī, who has the face of a sow, is in the center.
Consequently, by virtue of the location, Yamadaṃṣṭriṇī becomes Śūkarāsyā (Sow-faced).
Yamamathanī, who is Śūkarāsyā, becomes the Kulikā.
Thus, by the clockwise rotation starting from Kuṇḍalā, there is the movement during the solar portion.
Then, during the lunar portion, in the first watch after midday, there is the movement of Yamamathanī-Kulikā in the great cremation ground of Īśāna.
Vajravārāhī and Yamadāḍhī are in the center.
Then, by virtue of their positions, Yamamathanī becomes the Kulikā of Yamadāḍhī;
that which is Vajravārāhī-Yamadāḍhī becomes the Kulikā.
Then, during the second watch, there is the movement of Vajravārāhī, the Kulikā, in the great cremation ground of the northwest;
[and] Kākāsyā Yamadūtī is in the center. Consequently, by virtue of their respective positions, Vajravārāhī becomes Yamadūtī, and she who was Kākāsyā Yamadūtī becomes the Kulikā.
Then, during the third watch, there is the movement of Kākāsyā Kulikā in the great charnel ground of Nairṛtya,
and Ulūkāsyā Yamadaṃṣṭriṇī in the center.
Consequently, by virtue of their respective positions, Kākāsyā Kulikā becomes Yamadaṃṣṭriṇī.
She who is Ulūkāsyā-Yamadaṃṣṭriṇī is the Kulikā.
Therefore, in the fourth watch, there is the movement of the Kulikā Ulūkāsyā in the great cremation ground of Agni,
and of Śvānāsyā-Yamamathanī in the center.
Then, by virtue of their positions, Ulūkāsyā becomes Yamamathanī Kulikā;
she who was Śvānāsyā Yamamathanī becomes Kulikā.
Thus, by the counter-clockwise rotation of the earring, the movement of the Yoginīs occurs in the lunar portion.

On the seventh day, during the first watch from midnight at the great eastern cemetery, there is the movement of Śvānāsyā Kulikā. In the middle [watch], there is Śūkarāsyā and Kākāsyā; then, by virtue of the location, Śvānāsyā becomes Kulikā Kākāsyā, and she who was Śūkarāsyā becomes Kulikā.
Then, during the second watch, there is the movement of the sow-faced Kulikā in the southern great cremation ground;
that of Yamadāḍhī-Ulūkāsyā is in the center.
Consequently, by virtue of their respective locations, the sow-faced Kulikā becomes Ulūkāsyā.
Yamadāḍhī, who has the face of an owl, is the Kulikā;
therefore, during the third watch, the movement of Yamadāḍhī-Kulikā takes place in the western great cremation ground.
In the center of Yamadūtī and Śvānāsyā,
then, by virtue of their positions, Yamadāḍhī becomes Kulikā Śvānāsyā;
that which was Yamadūtī and Śvānāsyā becomes Kulikā.

Then, during the fourth watch, the Yamadūtī-kulikā wanders in the Northern Great Cremation Ground (Uttara-mahāśmaśāna). Between Yamadaṃṣṭriṇī and Śūkarāsyā, according to the sequence of locations, Yamadūtī becomes the Śūkarāsyā-kulikā;
that which was Yamadaṃṣṭriṇī becomes the Śūkarāsyā-kulikā.
Thus, by the clockwise rotation starting from Kuṇḍalā, the movement of the Yoginīs occurs during the solar portion.
Then, during the lunar portion, in the first watch after midday, the movement of Yamadaṃṣṭriṇī Kulikā occurs in the great cremation ground of Īśāna;
[the movement] of Yamamathanī and Yamadāḍhī occurs in the center.
Then, by virtue of the position, Yamadaṃṣṭriṇī becomes the Kulikā Yamadāḍhī;
and that Yamamathanī who was Yamadāḍhī becomes the Kulikā.
Thus, in the second watch, there is the movement of the Kulikā Yamamathanī in the great cremation ground of Vāyavya.
Vajravārāhī is Yamadūtī in the center.
Then, by virtue of her position, Yamamathanī becomes the Kulikā Yamadūtī;
that which is Vajravārāhī-Yamadūtī becomes the Kulikā.
Then, during the third watch, there is the movement of Vajravārāhī, the Kulikā, in the great cremation ground of Nairṛtya; Kākāsyā and Yamadaṃṣṭriṇī are in the center.
Consequently, due to the influence of the location, Vajravārāhī becomes Yamadaṃṣṭriṇī.
She who is Kākāsyā Yamadaṃṣṭriṇī is the Kulikā.
Therefore, in the fourth watch, there is the movement of the Kulikā Kākāsyā in the great cremation ground of Agni,
and that of Ulūkāsyā Yamamathanī in the center.
Then, by virtue of their positions, Kākāsyā becomes Yamamathanī Kulikā; and she who is Ulūkāsyā-Yamamathanī becomes Kulikā.

Thus, on the eighth day, the movement of Kuṇḍalā occurs in the leftward rotation within the lunar portion. Then, on the eighth day, from midnight during the first watch, there is the movement of Ulūkāsyā Kulikā in the eastern great cremation ground;
and that of Śvānāsyā and Kākāsyā is in the middle.
Then, by virtue of the position, Ulūkāsyā becomes the Kulikā Kākāsyā;
she who was Śvānāsyā becomes the Kulikā. Thereafter, in the second watch, there is the movement of Śvānāsyā, the Kulikā, in the great southern cremation ground.
Between the sow-faced and the owl-faced [goddesses] is the intermediate one.
Then, by virtue of their positions, the dog-faced goddess becomes the owl-faced Kulikā;
she who was the sow-faced becomes the firebrand-faced (ulka-āsyā) Kulikā.
Then, during the third watch, there is the movement of the sow-faced Kulikā in the western great cremation ground;
[the movement] of Yamadāḍhīśvānāsyā is in the center.
Then, by virtue of the location, the sow-faced one becomes the dog-faced one, and she who was Yamadāḍhīśvānāsyā becomes the Kulikā.
Then, during the fourth watch, there is the movement of Yamadāḍhī Kulikā in the northern great cremation ground;
[the movement] of Yamadūtī Śūkarāsyā is in the center.
Consequently, due to the influence of the location, Yamadāḍhī becomes Śūkarāsyā.
Yamadūtī, who has the face of a sow, is the Kulikā;

thus is the movement of the Yoginīs by the clockwise rotation of the earring during the solar portion. Then, during the lunar portion, in the first watch from midday, [the movement] of Yamadūtī-Kulikā is in the northeast—(45) mahāśma-... [text continues].
The movement is in Śāna.
Yamadaṃṣṭriṇī and Yamadāḍhī are in the center.
Then, by virtue of their positions, Yamadūtī becomes Kulikā and Yamadāḍhī.

Yamadaṃṣṭriṇī, who is Yamadāḍhī, is the Kulikā. Therefore, during the second watch, there is the movement of the Kulikā Yamadaṃṣṭriṇī in the great cremation ground of Vāyu (the northwest), while Yamamathani, who is Yamadūtī, is in the center.
Then, by virtue of the position, Yamadaṃṣṭriṇī becomes the Kulikā Yamadūtī;
that which is Yamamathanī-Yamadūtī becomes the Kulikā.
Then, during the third watch, there is the movement of the Kulikā Yamamathanī in the great charnel ground of Nairṛtya.
Vajravārāhī and Yamadaṃṣṭriṇī are in the center.
Then, by virtue of their positions, Yamamathanī becomes the Kulikā of Yamadaṃṣṭriṇī;
she who is Vajravārāhī-Yamadaṃṣṭriṇī becomes the Kulikā.
Then, during the fourth watch, there is the movement of the lineage-holder Vajravārāhī in the great cremation ground of Agni;
Kākāsyā Yamamathani is in the center.
Consequently, by virtue of the location, Vajravārāhī becomes Yamamathani as the lineage-holder.
Kākāsyā is Yamamathanī; she is the Kulikā.
Thus, by the counter-clockwise rotation of the earring, the movement of the Yoginīs occurs in the lunar portion.
On the ninth day, therefore, during the first watch from midnight, the movement of Kākāsyā-Kulikā takes place in the eastern great cremation ground.
Between Ulūkāsyā and Kākāsyā;
then, by virtue of her own place, Kākāsyā becomes Kulikā and so forth, and then again becomes Kākāsyā herself.
She who was Ulūkāsyā becomes Kulikā.
Then, during the second watch, there is the movement of Ulūkāsyā, the Kulikā, in the southern great cremation ground;
[the movement] of Śvānāsyā and Ulūkāsyā is in the center.
Then, by virtue of her own place, having become Ulūkāsyā, Kulikā, and so forth, she becomes Ulūkāsyā once again.
She who has the face of a dog and the face of an owl is the Kulikā.
Then, in the third watch, there is the movement of the dog-faced Kulikā in the western great cremation ground;
that of the sow-faced [Kulikā] is in the middle between the dog-faced and the owl-faced.

Then, by virtue of her own station, having become the Kulikā and others beginning with Śvānāsyā, she becomes Śvānāsyā once again; she who was Śūkarāsyā becomes Śvānāsyā, and she who was Kulikā becomes Śūkarāsyā.
Then, in the fourth watch, there is the movement of Śūkarāsyā-Kulikā in the northern Great Cremation Ground (Mahāśmaśāna), and that of Yamadāḍhī-Śūkarāsyā in the center.
Then, by virtue of her own position, having become Kulikā and the others, the Boar-faced one (Śūkarāsyā) becomes once again Śūkarāsyā.
That Yamadāḍhī who was Śūkarāsyā becomes Kulikā.
Thus, by the clockwise rotation of the Kundalī, is the movement of the Yoginīs during the solar portion.
Then, during the first watch from midday within the lunar portion, there is the movement of Yamadāḍhī Kulikā in the Īśāna Great Cremation Ground;
[the movement] of Yamadūtī in the center of Yamadāḍhī.
Then, by virtue of her own location, having become Yamadāḍhī, Kulikā, and so forth, she becomes Yamadāḍhī once again.
Yamadūtī, who possesses fierce fangs, is the Kulikā; therefore, during the second watch, the movement of Yamadūtī, the Kulikā,
takes place in the Vāyavya Great Cremation Ground.
Yamadaṃṣṭriṇī is in the center of Yamadūtī.
Then, by virtue of her own position, having become Kulikā and so forth, she becomes Yamadūtī again.
She who is Yamadaṃṣṭriṇī and Yamadūtī becomes Kulikā.
Then, during the third watch, there is the movement of Yamadaṃṣṭriṇī, the Kulikā, in the great charnel ground of Nairṛtya;
[the movement] of Yamadaṃṣṭriṇī and Yamamathanī is in the center.
Then, by virtue of her own place, having become Yamadaṃṣṭriṇī, Kulikā, and so forth, she becomes Yamadaṃṣṭriṇī once again.
She who is Yamamathanīyamadaṃṣṭriṇī is the Kulikā.
Therefore, during the fourth watch, there is the movement of the Kulikā Yamamathanī in the great cremation ground of Agni;
she is Vajravārāhī Yamamathanī in the center.
Then, by virtue of her own position, Yamamathanī becomes Kulikā and so forth, and subsequently becomes Yamamathānī again.
She who is Vajravārāhī becomes Kākāsyā and so forth, and then, by virtue of her own position, becomes Kulikā again.
Thus, the movement of the Yoginīs by way of the counter-clockwise rotation of the Kuṇḍalā should be understood by the Yogin within the lunar portion.

Thus, in the eight great cremation grounds, the movement of the Yoginīs according to the specific times constitutes the section on movement, [concluding] with their return to their respective places on the ninth day.
Then, having performed a magnificent worship, the movement on the tenth day is as it was on the first day;
on the eleventh day, it is as on the second day.
On the twelfth day, it is like the third;
on the thirteenth, like the fourth;
on the fourteenth, like the fifth.
On the new moon day, it is like the sixth;
on the first day of the waxing moon, it is like the seventh;
on the second day, it is like the eighth.
On the third day, the movement is like that of the ninth day.

Then, by virtue of returning to their respective abodes, Vajravārāhī and the others again assume their own individual natures. After performing the worship, there is again a movement on the fourth day, just as on the tenth day; and on the fifth day, it is like the eleventh day.
On the sixth day, it is like the twelfth;
on the seventh, like the thirteenth;
on the eighth, like the fourteenth.
On the ninth day it is like the new moon;
on the tenth day it is like the first day of the bright fortnight;
on the eleventh day it is like the second day.
On the twelfth day, there is a movement [of the deities] similar to that of the third day, according to the divisions of mind, speech, and body of the Śmaśānavāsinīs.
Thereafter, through nine new days and by conjunction with nine new lunar mansions (*nakṣatra*), the twenty-seven lunar mansions proceed until the moon reaches the end of the twelve zodiac signs.
Thus, through the fifteenfold division of the lunar digits (*kalā*), there is a movement of the Ḍākinīs and others together with Heruka.
The movement of Kākāsyā and the others occurs according to the division of the twenty-seven lunar mansions (*nakṣatra*).
Then, at the conclusion of the division of the Moon and Sun, the movement of Pracaṇḍā and the others takes place for three days.
It is as follows:

Regarding the movement of the wheels of mind, speech, and body (*citta-vāk-kāyacakrasaṃcāra*): here, on the thirteenth day of the waxing moon, at the rising of the sign of Scorpio, having performed worship at the eastern spoke of the *cittacakra*, there is a movement to the southern spoke of the means (*upāya*), which is *Pracaṇḍā*;
to the western spoke of *Caṇḍākṣī*; to the northern spoke of *Prabhāvatī*; and to the eastern spoke of *Mahānāsā*.

Then, by virtue of their positions, Pracaṇḍā becomes Caṇḍākṣī, Caṇḍākṣī becomes Prabhāvatī, Prabhāvatī becomes Mahānāsā, Mahānāsā becomes [the new] Pracaṇḍā, and [the former] Pracaṇḍā [becomes the new] Caṇḍākṣī.
Thereafter, in the half-interval of the scorpion, there is a transition of the former Pracaṇḍā to the western spoke;
a transition of the former Caṇḍākṣī to the northern spoke; a transition of the former Prabhāvatī to the eastern spoke; and a transition of the former Mahānāsā to the southern spoke.

Then, by virtue of their positions, Pracaṇḍā becomes Prabhāvatī, Caṇḍākṣī becomes Mahānāsā, Mahānāsā becomes Prabhāvatī, and Caṇḍākṣī becomes Pracaṇḍā. Thereafter, at the rising of the bow [constellation], there is the transition of the former Pracaṇḍā to the northern spoke, of the former Caṇḍākṣī to the eastern spoke, of the former Prabhāvatī to the southern spoke, and of the former Mahānāsā to the western spoke.

Then, by virtue of their positions, Pracaṇḍā becomes Mahānāsā, Caṇḍākṣī becomes Pracaṇḍā, Prabhāvatī becomes Caṇḍākṣī, and Mahānāsā becomes Prabhāvatī. Thereafter, during the half-month of Dhanus, the movement occurs as follows: from the previous Pracaṇḍā, there is movement to the eastern spoke; from Caṇḍākṣī to the southern spoke; from Prabhāvatī to the western spoke; and from Mahānāsā to the northern spoke.
Then, by virtue of their respective positions, the female messengers (dūtīs) beginning with Pracaṇḍā assume their own forms.
Thus, by means of a clockwise rotation starting from the right ear,

the movement of the four [messengers] must be performed in the circle of the assembly (gaṇacakra) during two and a half *daṇḍas* each, at the rising of Scorpio and the middle of Scorpio, and at the rising of Sagittarius and the middle of Sagittarius.

Then, when Makara has arisen, having performed worship, there is a transition for Vīramatī from the northeast petal to the northwest petal; for Kharvarī to the southwest petal; for Laṅkeśvarī to the southeast petal; and for Drumacchāyā to the northeast petal. Consequently, by virtue of their positions, Vīramatī becomes Kharvarī.

Kharvarī becomes Laṅkeśvarī; Laṅkeśvarī becomes Drumacchāyā; Drumacchāyā becomes Vīramatī. Then, in the half-circle of the crocodile [mandala], there is a transposition from the previous Vīramatī to the southwestern spoke. There is a transposition from the previous Kharvarī to the southeastern spoke, from the previous Laṅkeśvarī to the northeastern spoke, and from the previous Drumacchāyā to the northwestern spoke. Consequently, by virtue of their positions, Vīramatī becomes Laṅkeśvarī, Kharvarī becomes Drumacchāyā, Laṅkeśvarī becomes Vīramatī, and Drumacchāyā becomes Kharvarī.

Then, at the rising of Kumbha, there is a transition of Pūrvavīramatī to the southeast spoke, of Pūrvakharvarī to the northeast spoke, of Pūrvalaṅkeśvarī to the northwest spoke, and of Pūrvadrumacchāyā to the southwest spoke. Consequently, by virtue of their positions, Vīramatī becomes Drumacchāyā, and Kharvarī becomes Vīramatī.
Laṅkeśvarī becomes Kharvarī;
Drumacchāyā becomes Laṅkeśvarī. Then, in the half-vase [of the northeast], there is the movement of Pūrvavīramatī into the northeast spoke.
The movement of Pūrvakharvarī occurs at the northwest spoke; the movement of Pūrvalaṅkeśvarī occurs at the southwest spoke; and the movement of Pūrvadrumacchāyā occurs at the southeast spoke.
Then, by virtue of their respective positions, the Yoginīs beginning with Vīramatī assume their own forms.

Thus, through the counter-clockwise rotation of Kuṇḍalā, the movement of the Yoginīs takes place during the rising of Capricorn and the half of Capricorn, and during the rising of Aquarius and the half of Aquarius.
Thus, by means of the division of the half-lagna, the movement of the eight Yoginīs within the mind-wheel (*cittacakra*) in the *gaṇacakra* is to be understood by the yogins.
(48) Then, having performed the worship, the movement within the speech-wheel (*vākcakra*) should be carried out. It is as follows:
Here, at the rising of the sign Pisces, there is the movement of Airāvatī from the eastern spoke of the wheel of speech to the southern spoke;
that of Mahābhairavā to the western spoke;
that of Vāyuvegā to the northern spoke; and the movement of Surabhākṣī occurs in the eastern spoke.
Then, by virtue of their positions, Airāvatī becomes Mahābhairavā;

or Mahābhairavā becomes Vāyuvegā; Vāyuvegā becomes Surābhakṣī; and Surābhakṣī becomes Airāvatī. Thereafter, during the half-period of Mīna, there is a transference: from the eastern Airāvatī to the western spoke, from the eastern Mahābhairavā to the northern spoke, from the eastern Vāyuvegā to the eastern spoke, and from the eastern Surābhakṣī to the southern spoke. This is the transference that occurs.

Then, by virtue of their positions, Airāvatī becomes Vāyuvegā; Mahābhairavā becomes Surābhakṣī; Vāyuvegā becomes Airāvatī; and Surābhakṣī becomes Mahābhairavā. Then, at the rising of Aries, there is a transference from the eastern Airāvatī to the northern spoke, from the eastern Mahābhairavā to the eastern spoke, from the eastern Vāyuvegā to the southern spoke, and from the eastern Surābhakṣī to the western spoke.
Then, by virtue of their positions, Airāvatī becomes Surābhakṣī; Mahābhairavā becomes Airāvatī; Vāyuvegā becomes Mahābhairavā; and Surābhakṣī becomes Vāyuvegā.

Then, in the eastern spoke of Airāvatī during the latter half of Aries, there is the movement of Pūrvā; in the southern spoke, that of Pūrvamahābhairavā; in the western spoke, that of Pūrvavāyuvegā; and in the northern spoke, that of Pūrvasurābhakṣyā.
Thereafter, by virtue of their respective locations, Airāvatī and the others assume their own individual forms.
Thus, by means of the clockwise rotation of the *kuṇḍalī*, the movement of the four Yoginīs occurs in the Wheel of Speech (*vākcakra*) through the division of the halves of the zodiacal signs.

Then, having performed the worship at the rising of the bull-lagna (*vṛṣalagnodaya*), the movement of Śyāmādevī occurs from the northeast (*īśāna*) to the northwest (*vāyavya*); that of Subhadrā from the southwest (*nairṛtya*) to the southeast (*āgneya*); and that of Hayakarṇā from the southeast to the northeast.
Consequently, due to the influence of their respective positions, Śyāmādevī becomes Subhadrā; Subhadrā becomes Hayakarṇā; Hayakarṇā becomes Khagānanā; and Khagānanā becomes Śyāmādevī.

Then, during the first half of the bull [lagna], there is a transposition (*saṃcāra*): Śyāmādevī moves from the eastern spoke to the south-western spoke; Subhadrā from the eastern spoke to the south-eastern spoke; Hayakarṇā from the eastern spoke to the north-eastern spoke; and Khagānanā from the eastern spoke to the north-western spoke.
Consequently, by virtue of their positions, Śyāmādevī becomes Hayakarṇā, Subhadrā becomes Khagānanā, Hayakarṇā becomes Śyāmādevī, and Khagānanā becomes Subhadrā.

Then, at the rising of the Gemini [lagna], there is a transposition: Śyāmādevī moves from the eastern spoke to the south-eastern spoke; Subhadrā from the eastern spoke to the north-eastern spoke; Hayakarṇā from the eastern spoke to the north-western spoke; and Khagānanā moves from the eastern spoke to the south-western spoke.

Then, by virtue of their respective positions, Śyāmādevī becomes Khagānanā and Subhadrā becomes Hayakarṇā; [likewise] Subhadrā becomes Khagānanā and Hayakarṇā becomes Śyāmādevī. Thereafter, during the first half of the *mithuna* (twelfth) lunar mansion, there occurs a transposition (*saṃcāra*): Śyāmādevī moves from her eastern position to the northeast spoke, Subhadrā from the east to the northwest spoke, Hayakarṇā from the east to the southwest spoke, and Khagānanā from the east to the southeast spoke. Then, by virtue of their own respective positions, the yoginīs beginning with Śyāmādevī assume their own original forms.
Thus, the movement of the four yoginīs occurs in the wheel of speech (*vākcakra*) by means of the counter-clockwise rotation starting from Kuṇḍalā.
The movement of the eight yoginīs in the wheel of the assembly (*gaṇacakra*) should be performed according to the division of the half-signs beginning with Pisces (*mīna*).
(49) Then, having performed the worship, the movement in the wheel of body (*kāyacakre*) should be performed.
For example:

here, at the rising of Cancer, there is a transition from the eastern spoke of the body wheel (*kāyacakra*) to the southern spoke of Cakravegā, to the western spoke of Khaṇḍarohā, to the northern spoke of Śauṇḍinī, and to the eastern spoke of Cakravarmiṇī.
Then, by virtue of their positions, Cakravegā becomes Khaṇḍarohā, Khaṇḍarohā becomes Śauṇḍinī, Śauṇḍinī becomes Cakravarmiṇī, and Cakravarmiṇī becomes Cakravegā.

Then, in the western spoke of the eastern *cakravegā* in the Karkaṭārdha [mandala], there is the movement of *pūrvakhaṇḍarohā*; in the northern spoke, that of *pūrvaśauṇḍinī*; in the eastern spoke, that of *pūrvacakravarmiṇī*; and in the southern spoke, that of *pūrvacakravegā*. Then, by virtue of their positions, *pūrvacakravegā* becomes *śauṇḍinī*, *pūrvakhaṇḍarohā* becomes *cakravarmiṇī*, *pūrvaśauṇḍinī* becomes *cakravegā*, and *pūrvacakravarmiṇī* becomes *khaṇḍarohā*.

Then, at the rising of the constellation Siṃha (Leo), there is a transference to the northern spoke of Pūrvacakravegā; to the eastern spoke of Pūrvakhaṇḍarohā; to the southern spoke of Pūrvaśauṇḍinī; and to the western spoke of Pūrvacakravarmiṇī. Consequently, by virtue of their positions, Pūrvacakravegā becomes Cakravarmiṇī; Pūrvakhaṇḍarohā becomes Cakravegā; Pūrvaśauṇḍinī becomes Khaṇḍarohā; and Pūrvacakravarmiṇī becomes Śauṇḍinī.

Then, in the half-siṃha [position], there is the movement of Pūrvacakravegā on the eastern spoke, Pūrvakhaṇḍarohā on the southern spoke, Pūrvaśauṇḍinī on the western spoke, and Pūrvacakravarmiṇī on the northern spoke. Thereafter, by virtue of their respective positions, the yoginīs beginning with Cakravegā assume their own forms.
Thus is the movement in the body-wheel (kāyacakra) by means of the clockwise rotation of the kuṇḍalī.

Then, having performed the worship, the movement should be carried out by way of counter-clockwise rotation (*vāmāvarta*). It is as follows: here, at the rising of the sign of Virgo (*kanyālagna*), the movement of Suvīrā begins from the northeast spoke (*īśānāra*); that of Mahābalā occurs at the northwest spoke (*vāyavyāra*); that of Cakravartinī at the southwest spoke (*nairṛtyāra*); that of Mahāvīryā at the southeast spoke (*āgneyāra*); and [finally] the movement of [Suvīrā] occurs at the northeast spoke (*īśānāra*).

Then, by virtue of their positions, Suvīrā becomes Mahābalā; Mahābalā becomes Cakravartinī; Cakravartinī becomes Mahāvīryā; and Mahāvīryā becomes Suvīrā. Thereafter, in the half of the [remaining] maiden, there is a transposition: Suvīrā from the east moves to the southwest spoke; Mahābalā from the east moves to the southeast spoke; Cakravartinī from the east moves to the northeast spoke; and Mahāvīryā from the east moves to the northwest spoke. Then, by virtue of their positions, Suvīrā becomes Cakravartinī.
She is of great heroism and great strength; she is a sovereign wheel-turner, well-heroic,
and becomes one of great heroism and great strength.
Then, at the rising of the Libra ascendant, there is the movement of Pūrvasuvīrā to the southeast spoke,
of Pūrvamahābalā to the northeast spoke, and of Pūrvacakravartinī to the northwest spoke.
The movement of Pūrvamahāvīryā occurs in the southwestern spoke (nairṛtyāra). Thereafter, by virtue of the shift in position, Suvīrā becomes Mahāvīryā, and Mahābalā becomes Suvīrā.
The female universal monarch (cakravartinī) possesses great strength;
she becomes a female universal monarch through great heroism.
Then, at the midpoint of the scale, there is a movement from Pūrvasuvīrā to the northeast (īśāna) spoke.
The movement [of the goddesses] is as follows: Pūrvamahābalā is on the northwest spoke; Pūrvacakravartinī is on the southwest spoke;
and Pūrvamahāvīryā is on the southeast spoke.
Then, by virtue of their respective positions, the four yoginīs, Suvīrā and the others, assume their own individual forms.
Thus is the movement [of the breath] by means of the counter-clockwise rotation of Kuṇḍalī.
In the body wheel (kāyacakra), the movement of the yoginīs in the circle of the assembly (gaṇacakra) should be performed according to the divisions of the half-signs beginning with Virgo (Kanyā).

Thus, on the first day, there is the movement of the Yoginīs through twenty-four divisions consisting of the halves of the twelve zodiac signs, such as Scorpio and so forth; this occurs on the thirteenth [tithi],
here according to the division of the mind or the division of the quality of tamas on the thirteenth day.
Likewise, on the fourteenth day, or on the second day, by means of the differentiation of speech or the differentiation of the *rajas* quality;
and thus on the full moon day, or on the third day, by means of the differentiation of body or the differentiation of the *sattva* quality—

the movement of the twenty-four Yoginīs must be performed by the yogins in the *gaṇacakra*, according to the twenty-four divisions of time within the twelve half-signs (*ardhalagna*) beginning with Scorpio.

Thus is the rule for the procedure of the movement of the Yoginīs according to the twenty-four specific times. Here, whichever Yoginī moves to whichever place, by virtue of consuming her leftovers and by adopting the means (upāya) of her family,
she becomes of that family until she returns to her own place.
Then, by returning to her own place, she becomes established in her own family (*kula*).

Thus, by the grasping of Heruka through the power of consuming the remnants of the *Kulikā*, whichever *ḍākinī* or yoginī from Yamamathanī onwards enters into the center, she becomes the *Kulikā* Vajravārāhī.
And she who is the *Kulikā* Vajravārāhī becomes a member of that family (*tatkulinī*) by the power of consuming the remnants of others.

Thus, by virtue of their respective locations, the thirty-six yoginīs of the families (kulayoginīs) who are non-familial (akulīnāḥ) become familial (kulīnāḥ), and those who are familial become non-familial.

Just as, according to worldly convention (*laukika-saṃvṛti*), even those of low birth become of noble birth for Brahmins and others once they have been bathed beneath the jeweled parasol of a universal monarch (*cakravartin*);

and just as Viśvāmitra and others, though born from the wombs of outcaste dog-cookers and thus of low birth, became Brahmins through the power of mantra, meditation, and austerity— likewise, even Brahmins of noble birth become of low birth by eating beef and the like, or by eating in the houses of outcastes such as Caṇḍālas.

Likewise, in the *Yoginīsaṃcāra*, by means of visiting other locations, eating, consuming, and grasping, the yoginīs previously mentioned— thirty-seven in number, beginning with Ḍombī— are to be known by the yogins according to worldly convention for the purpose of moving within the *gaṇacakra* as family messengers (*kuladūtī*). Thus, having performed worship, mantra recitation, and meditation for three years, one performs the fire sacrifice (*homa*) at the conclusion of the mantra recitation.
Then, for as long as three fortnights, one should perform the movement of the Yoginīs within the *gaṇacakra*.

Thereafter, all that was previously mentioned regarding the means of attaining worldly accomplishments (*laukikasiddhi*) as taught in the Tantras will always and in every way be accomplished by the practitioner.
Furthermore, by another method, a single accomplishment is achieved through a single rite, namely by means of mantra-recitation, meditation, and fire-offerings (*homa*).

Furthermore, a yogi does not achieve the accomplishment of the *pradhāna* (the primary goal) through the accomplishment of a single rite, nor through the accomplishment of a single [magical] power such as the sword (*khaḍga*) or other such powers.
Therefore, this movement of the Yoginīs (*yoginīsaṃcāra*) must be understood by yogis according to the specific times [prescribed] in the *Mūlatantra* known as the *Lakṣābhidhāna*;
or else, it has been explained here by means of this commentary.
Thus is the rule for the direct realization of the expansion of all worldly activities and all accomplishments, and for the attainment of the state of a great adept (*mahāsiddha*).
This is the procedure for the movement of the Yoginīs.

(51) Chapter IX: The Development of the Locations Now, the seats—which are the transformations of the seed-syllables of the locations and names—are described both internally and externally, as well as in the *gaṇacakra*.

Therein, externally, below Mount Meru is the mandala of space, transformed from the syllable *haṃ*; internally, it is the pericarp of the lotus at the crown of the head (*uṣṇīṣa*). Externally, above that is the mandala of wind, transformed from the syllable *yaṃ*; internally, it is the pericarp of the lotus at the forehead.
Externally, above that, is the fire mandala transformed from the syllable *raṃ*; internally, it is the pericarp of the throat lotus.
Externally, above that, is the water mandala transformed from the syllable *vaṃ*; internally, it is the pericarp of the heart lotus.
Externally, above that, is the earth mandala transformed from the syllable *laṃ*; internally, it is the pericarp of the navel lotus.

Externally, above that, is Mount Meru, transformed from the syllable *maṃ*; internally, it is the pericarp of the secret lotus. Externally, above that, is the universal lotus, transformed from the syllable *kṣaṃ*; internally, it consists of the eight channels together with the pericarp located within the vajra-jewel.
On the pericarp externally is the solar disc; internally, it is the fire of time (*kālāgni*).
Externally, above that, are Umā and Maheśvara; internally, they are the *rajas* and *śukra* located therein.
Externally, above that, is Heruka; internally, he is the innate bliss (*sahajānanda*) that arises when those two have been restrained through non-emission externally.
Vajravārāhī possesses an indestructible nature, like the moonlight of the moon of omniscience arising from the radiance of his rays.
Thus, by way of body, speech, and mind at the navel, the secret place, and the vajra-jewel, the Lord Heruka is called Sahajānanda (Innate Bliss).
Here, Sahajānanda is the fourth, the Gnosis-Vajra. In this way, the Lord Heruka has four faces, consisting of the faces of body, speech, mind, and gnosis.
By the very nature of those four faces, the thirty-six Ḍākinīs abide upon the spokes of the wheels in the north, south, east, and west.

The corpse-seats (*śavāsana*) are formed by the transformation of the first syllable of each of their own names and locations. On the outside, in the front of the Knowledge Wheel (*jñānacakra*), there is a *preta* transformed from the letter *Ā*; within, in the navel lotus, there are sixty channels (*nāḍī*) that carry the mandalas and four twilight-channels (*saṃdhyānāḍī*).
When the vital wind (*prāṇavāyu*) is restrained within those channels, starting with the eastern one, it is called the "corpse-seat."

Thus, on the outer [wheel], on the southern spoke is that which has transformed from the syllable *paṃ*, belonging to Lāmā; on the western spoke, that which has transformed from the syllable *maṃ*, belonging to Khaṇḍarohā; and on the northern [spoke], that which has transformed from the syllable *taṃ*, belonging to Rūpiṇī.
Thus, in the intermediate directions of the Jñānacakra are the skull-bowls of feces, urine, blood, and flesh.

(52) On the eight great cremation grounds on the outside, in the eastern cremation ground is a corpse-seat transformed from the syllable *śūṃ*, belonging to Kākāsyā; internally, this corresponds to the cessation of the vital wind (*prāṇavāyu*) in the channel of the mouth.

Likewise, externally, the transformation of the syllable *śaṃ* is [the seat] of Ulūkāsyā in the south; internally, it is the cessation of the vital breath (*prāṇa*) in the channel of the right nostril.
Externally, the transformation of the syllable *pūṃ* is [the seat] of Śvānāsyā in the west; internally, it is the restraint of the downward-voiding wind (*apāna*) in the channel of the anus.
Externally, the transformation of the syllable *kleṃ* is [the seat] of Śūkarāsyā on the northern spoke; internally, it is the restraint of the vital breath in the channel of the left nostril.

Externally, in the northeast, there is a corpse-seat transformed from the syllable *bāṃ*, belonging to Yamadāḍhī; internally, it is the cessation of the vital breath (*prāṇa*) in the left ear channel.
Externally, in the northwest, there is a corpse transformed from the syllable *saṃ*, belonging to Yamadūtī; internally, it is the cessation of the vital breath in the right ear channel.
Externally, in the southwest, there is [a corpse] transformed from the syllable *ghoṃ*, belonging to Yamadaṃṣṭriṇī; internally, it is the cessation of the vital breath in the right eye channel.
Externally, [the seat] in the southeast is the transformation of the syllable *uṃ*; internally, it is the cessation of the vital breath (*prāṇa*) in the channel of the left eye for Yamamathanī.
Thus, the eight great cremation grounds that serve as seats for Kākāsyā and the others are to be understood externally in the *gaṇacakra*.

Now, the seats of Pracaṇḍā and the others, which are the transformations of the seed-syllables of their respective locations and names, are described. Here, in the outer *cittacakra*, upon the eastern spoke, there is a corpse seat transformed from the syllable *pūṃ*; this is for Pracaṇḍā. In the inner *dharmacakra*, it is the cessation of the vital breath (*prāṇa*) in the eastern channel; according to the definitive meaning (*nītārtha*).
According to the interpretable meaning (*neyārtha*), it is the placement of the syllable *pūṃ* on the head externally.

Thus, externally, on the southern spoke, there is a corpse transformed from the syllable *jāṃ*, which belongs to Caṇḍākṣī; internally, it signifies the cessation of the vital breath (*prāṇa*) in the right channel—this is the definitive meaning (*nītārtha*).
According to the interpretable meaning (*neyārtha*), the placement of the syllable *jāṃ* is at the crest-lock (*śikhā*).
Externally, on the western spoke, there is a corpse transformed from the syllable *oṃ*, which belongs to Prabhāvatī; internally, it signifies the cessation of the vital breath in the western channel.
According to the interpretable meaning (*neyārtha*), the placement of the syllable *oṃ* is above the right ear.

On the outer northern spoke, there is a corpse transformed from the syllable *aṃ*; internally, this corresponds to the cessation of the vital breath (*prāṇa*) in the northern channel of the great nose. At the heart, the wheel of dharma (*dharmacakra*), according to the interpretable meaning, the placement of the syllable *aṃ* is on the back of the neck.
This is the placement of the seed-syllables of the sacred seats (*pīṭha*).

Likewise, externally, on the eastern spoke of the mind-wheel (*cittacakra*), there is the corpse transformed from the syllable *goṃ*, which serves as the seat for Vīramatī; internally, in the dharma-wheel (*dharmacakra*), it is the cessation of the vital breath (*prāṇa*) in the eastern channel (*nāḍī*).

According to the interpretable meaning (*neyārtha*), the placement of the syllable *goṃ* is above the left ear. Externally, on the northwest spoke, there is the corpse transformed from the syllable *rāṃ*, which serves as the seat for Kharvarī; internally, it is the cessation of the vital breath in the northwest channel.
According to the interpretable meaning (*neyārtha*), there is the placement of the syllable *rāṃ* between the eyebrows.

Externally, on the southwestern spoke, there is a corpse transformed from the syllable *deṃ*, which belongs to Laṅkeśvarī; internally, it is the cessation of the vital breath (*prāṇa*) within the southwestern channel (*nāḍī*).
According to the interpretable meaning, there is the placement of the syllable *deṃ* upon the two eyes.

Externally, on the southeast spoke, there is a corpse transformed from the syllable *māṃ*, situated in the shade of a tree; internally, it is the cessation of the vital breath (*prāṇa*) in the southeast channel at the wheel of dharma (*dharmacakra*).
In the sense of the "to-be-guided" (*neyārtha*), the placement of the syllable *māṃ* is at the base of the arm.
Thus is the rule for the seats of the goddesses of the secondary sites (*upapīṭha*) within the wheel of mind (*cittacakra*).

Then, regarding the outer speech-wheel (*vākcakra*), which is the enjoyment wheel (*saṃbhogacakra*) within, there are thirty-two channels in the outer circle and eight channels in the inner circle; as in the case of the dharma-wheel, the seats here are likewise described.

On the eastern spoke of the outer speech-wheel, the seat of Airāvatī is a corpse transformed from the syllable *kāṃ*; within, on the eastern channel of the inner circle of the enjoyment wheel, there is the cessation of the vital breath (*prāṇa*).
According to the interpretable meaning (*neyārtha*), there is the placement of the syllable *oṃ* on the two armpits.
On the outer right spoke is a corpse transformed from the syllable *oṃ*, which is Mahābhairavī; internally, this is the cessation of the vital breath (*prāṇa*) in the right channel (*nāḍī*).
According to the interpretable meaning, there is the placement of the syllable *oṃ* on the pair of breasts.
Externally, on the western spoke, there is a corpse transformed from the syllable *triṃ*; internally, this is the cessation of the vital breath (*prāṇa*) in the western channel of Vāyuvegā.
According to the interpretable meaning (*neyārtha*), it is the placement of the syllable *triṃ* at the navel.
Externally, on the northern spoke, there is a corpse transformed from the syllable *koṃ*; internally, this is the cessation of the vital breath in the northern channel of Surābhakṣī.

According to the interpretable meaning (*neyārtha*), the placement of the syllable *kaṃ* on the tip of the nose is the placement of the seed-syllables for the seats of the goddesses of the fields and sub-fields within the wheel of speech (*vākcakra*).

Likewise, externally, on the eastern spoke (*īśānāra*), there is the seat of the goddess Śyāmā, which is a corpse transformed from the syllable *kaṃ*; internally, in the wheel of the throat (*kaṇṭhacakra*), it is the cessation of the vital breath (*prāṇa*) in the eastern channel (*īśānanāḍī*).
According to the interpretable meaning, the placement of the syllable *kaṃ* is in the mouth.

Externally, on the northwest spoke, there is a corpse transformed from the syllable *laṃ*, belonging to Subhadrā; internally, it is the cessation of the vital breath (*prāṇa*) in the northwest channel (*nāḍī*).
According to the interpretable meaning (*neyārtha*), this is the placement of the syllable *laṃ* at the throat.
Externally, on the southwest spoke, there is a corpse transformed from the syllable *kāṃ*, belonging to Hayakarṇā; internally, it is the cessation of the vital breath in the southwest channel.
According to the provisional meaning (*neyārtha*), there is the placement of the syllable *kāṃ* in the heart;

externally, on the southeast spoke, there is a corpse-seat transformed from the syllable *hiṃ*, which serves as the seat for Khagānanā. Internally, it is the restraint of the vital breath (*prāṇavāyu*) within the southeast channel (*nāḍī*).
According to the provisional meaning, there is the placement of the syllable *hiṃ* at the genitals.
Thus is the placement of the seed-syllables for the seats of the *Chandoha* and *Upachandoha* *Ḍākinīs* within the *Saṃbhoga-vākcakra*.

Such is the rule for the seats of the goddesses of the *Kṣetra*, *Upakṣetra*, *Chandoha*, and *Upachandoha*. Then, regarding the *Kāyacakram*: externally, on the forehead, in the *Sahajacakra*; externally, in the circular [mandala], there are sixteen channels;
internally, in the circular [mandala], there are eight channels. Just as in the *Saṃbhogacakra*, so too here the seats are described.

Here, in the external body-wheel (*kāyacakra*), upon the eastern spoke, there is a corpse-seat transformed from the syllable *preṃ*, which belongs to Cakravega. Internally, in the innate wheel (*sahajacakra*), within the inner circle, it is the cessation of the vital wind (*prāṇavāyu*) in the eastern channel.
According to the interpretable meaning (*neyārtha*), the syllable *preṃ* is placed upon the male organ (*liṅga*).

Externally, on the southern spoke, there is a corpse transformed from the syllable *GṚṂ*, belonging to Khaṇḍarohā; internally, it is the cessation of the vital breath (*prāṇa*) in the right channel (*nāḍī*). According to the interpretable meaning (*neyārtha*), it is the placement of the syllable *GṚṂ* at the anus. Externally, on the western spoke, there is a corpse transformed from the syllable *SAUṂ*, belonging to Śauṇḍinī; internally, it is the cessation of the vital wind in the western channel. According to the interpretable meaning, it is the placement of the syllable *SAUṂ* on the pair of thighs.

Externally, on the northern spoke, there is a corpse transformed from the syllable *suṃ*, which belongs to Cakravarmiṇī; internally, it is the cessation of the vital breath (*prāṇa*) in the northern channel.
According to the interpretable meaning (*neyārtha*), it is the placement of the syllable *suṃ* upon the two shanks.
Thus is the placement of the seats and seed-syllables for the messengers (*dūtī*) of the assembly (*melāpaka*) and the non-assembly (*upamelāpaka*) within the body wheel (*kāyacakra*).

Then, here on the outside, upon the spoke of Īśāna, there is a corpse-seat transformed from the syllable *naṃ*, which is the seat of Suvīrā; internally, it is the cessation of the vital breath (*prāṇa*) in the Īśāna channel.

According to the definitive meaning (*nītārtha*), this refers to the cessation of the breath; according to the interpretable meaning (*neyārtha*), it is the placement of the syllable *naṃ* on the toes.
On the outside, upon the spoke of Vāyu, there is a corpse transformed from the syllable *siṃ*, which is the seat of Mahābalā; internally, it is the cessation of the vital breath in the Vāyu channel.
According to the provisional meaning (*neyārtha*), there is the placement of the syllable *siṃ* on the backs of the feet.

On the outer rim of the southwest spoke, there is a corpse transformed from the syllable *maṃ*, which belongs to Cakravartinī; in the internal sense, this is the cessation of the vital breath (*prāṇavāyu*) in the southwest channel (*nāḍī*).
According to the provisional meaning, there is the placement of the syllable *maṃ* on the two big toes.

Externally, on the southeast spoke, there is a corpse-seat transformed from the syllable *kuṃ*, which is the seat of Mahāvīryā; internally, it is the cessation of the vital breath (*prāṇa*) in the southeastern channel.
According to the interpretable meaning (*neyārtha*), it is the placement of the seed-syllable *kuṃ* upon both knees.
Thus is the placement of the seats and seed-syllables for the goddesses of the cremation grounds and sub-cremation grounds within the body wheel (*kāyacakra*).

Thus, in the body wheel (*kāyacakra*), there is a fixed arrangement of seats for those who dwell in the meeting places (*melāpaka*), secondary meeting places (*upamelāpaka*), charnel grounds (*śmaśāna*), and secondary charnel grounds (*upaśmaśāna*).

Here, just as externally the *ḍākinīs* have vehicles of corpses for the purpose of traveling to the sacred sites (*pīṭha*) and so forth, so internally all the elements have the vital wind (*prāṇavāyu*) as their vehicle.

Just as externally, in the gathering of the assembly (*gaṇamelāpaka*), corpses are situated upon their respective wheel-spokes (*cakrāra*), so internally the vital winds are situated within the channels (*nāḍī*) of their respective wheels by means of the yoga of breath retention (*kumbhaka*). This is the definitive meaning (*nītārtha*).

Here, in the external *gaṇacakra*, having consecrated the seats of the thirty-six dūtīs with the aforementioned seed-syllables seven times for the sake of purifying the human skin and the corpse, they should be placed upon their respective locations.
Such is the procedure for the seats: for the Lord and the Prajñā, a tiger skin and a leopard skin are in the center.
Here, in the *gaṇacakra*, the generation of Pracaṇḍā and the others, as well as Ḍākinī and the others, occurs through the seed-syllables of their own names and so forth.
The rule in all tantras is that one should effect the transfer from place to place by consecrating with that very same seed-syllable.

(55) Chapter X: The Pills of Secret Elements Now, the *samayaguḍikā* (vow-pill) is described for the purpose of purifying the mouth and other [senses]. Here, the five nectars (*pañcāmṛta*) and the five lamps (*pañcapradīpa*) are to be taken according to the distinction of the increasing qualities of each element, beginning with space, when there is an eclipse of both the moon and the sun within a single month—first that of the moon and subsequently that of the sun in that month, and not first that of the sun and subsequently that of the moon in that month.

In this context, during a lunar eclipse at the time of the first day of the lunar fortnight (*pratipad*), one should worship a twelve-year-old or sixteen-year-old maiden who has not yet borne children—a *gaurī*—with all necessary ritual implements. Having established her as the focal point for the deity, one should insert the *vajra* into the lotus and, with the utterance of *hūṃ phaṭ*, emit the *bodhicitta*.
Having emitted it, one should place a lotus-vessel below and, drawing it up with the *vajra*, pour it into that lotus-vessel.
On the second day, having performed worship to a corpse, marrow should be taken.
On the third day, having performed worship to a non-Aryan woman who is menstruating, Ratnasambhava should be taken. On the fourth day, one’s own vajra-water should be taken.
From the five [elements], feces is to be taken.

Thus, one *māṣaka* of semen, two *māṣakas* of marrow, three *māṣakas* of Ratnasaṃbhava, four *māṣakas* of Vajrodaka, and five *māṣakas* of Vairocana; in this way, through the increase of one, two, three, four, and five qualities respectively for space, wind, fire, water, and earth, the five substances are to be collected over five days.
Then, having performed the worship of the deceased on the sixth day, human flesh should be taken;
on the seventh, horse flesh; on the eighth, elephant flesh; on the ninth, dog flesh; and on the tenth, cow flesh.
[These should be] the measure of one eye, the measure of two eyes, the measure of three eyes, the measure of four eyes, and the measure of five eyes.

Having taken the lamp in due order and combined it with the five nectars (*pañcāmṛta*) in a measure of seventy-five *māṣakas*, one should then, on the eleventh day before eating, drink as much liquor as desired— whether honey-wine (*mādhvī*), molasses-wine (*gauḍī*), grape-wine (*drākṣī*), wine from trees such as the palmyra, wine from fermented grain (*dhānyaja*), or flour-wine (*paiṣṭhī*)— together with fifteen *makṣikā* drops of nectar. (56)
One should cause her to vomit.
With that vomit collected in a skull-cup, one should grind those ten substances consisting of seventy-five māṣakas.
Then, having taken a jackal’s skull, one should place [the powder] inside it.

Then, having joined the two halves of a skull-cup as a vessel, at that very time of night in a cremation ground, one should dig a single hand-deep triangular pit in the ground where a woman who entered the fire together with a dead man was burned.
Having worshipped there with perfumes, incense, and so forth, and having offered a most magnificent *bali* offering, [one should act] according to this mantra procedure:
*oṃ vajrakrodheśvari sarvadravyāṇi viśodhaya hūṃ phaṭ*.
Thus ends the mantra for purifying the bali offering.
May the Buddhas, the fathers together with their mothers, along with their sons, servants, and circles of kinsmen, arrive—
surrounded by the entire host of divine deities and bringing satisfaction to the sublime Vajrasattva.
Thus is the invocation of all the Tathāgatas.
Oṃ śrīheruka ākaṭṭaya ākaṭṭaya praveśaya praveśaya bandhaya bandhaya toṣaya toṣaya sarvaḍākinīnāṃ hṛdayaṃ jaḥ hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ hūṃ phaṭ.
This is the mantra for summoning the ḍākinīs.
Oṃ sumbha niḥsumbha hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ | Oṃ gṛhṇa gṛhṇa hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ | Oṃ gṛhṇāpaya gṛhṇāpaya hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ | Oṃ ānaya ho bhagavān vajravidyārāja hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ |
Thus ends the mantra for the offering of the bali.
Then, having offered the water for honor (*argha*), the water for the feet (*pādya*), and so forth,
one should empower [the materials] one hundred and eight times with this mantra: *oṃ śrīvajra he he ru ru kaṃ huṃ hūṃ phaṭ ḍākinījālasaṃvaraṃ svāhā*, and cast them into that pit.
One should fill a pit at the head [of the corpse] with funeral ashes and offer a great lion [seat]. (57) Oṃ vajravairocanīye svāhā.
Having performed the protection ritual with this mantra and returned to one's own home, one should recite the Caturvaktra-mantra at the four junctions of the day on the twelfth lunar day;
the eight-line version on the thirteenth;
and the twenty-four-line version on the fourteenth.
Then, on the new moon day during a solar eclipse, having extracted [the substance], one should fashion pills the size of mung beans with human fat.
By means of that pill, food, drink, and so forth—when sprinkled together with the *kuṇḍagolaka*—become purified.
When placed in the mouth, purification of the mouth occurs.
At the time of the gaṇacakra and even during the period of meditative cultivation, there is protection from all [harm]. Thus is the rule for the procedure of the pill (gulikā).

(58) Chapter XI: The Rite of Food and Drink in the Gaṇacakra Now, the procedure for the food and drink of the thirty-six family messengers (*kuladūtī*), beginning with the *ḍombī* and the *śūdrī*, as previously mentioned, in the great *gaṇacakra* is described.

Here, in a secluded house or a well-concealed place, all the family messengers are naked, and the twenty-four practitioners (*sādhaka*) are adorned with the five seals (*pañcamudrā*). In their respective places, the yoginīs have their hair loose, while the practitioners have their hair tied in topknots.
They are seated upon human skins.
The Lord of the Gaṇas is in the center of the wheel, upon a cowhide and a tiger skin.
Then, having made a hand-sized mat from human skin, one should give it to the Leader of the Gaṇas.

One should give a strip of horse-hide to the yoginīs of the east, a strip of dog-hide to the yoginīs of the south, a strip of elephant-hide to the yoginīs of the west, and a strip of cow-hide to the yoginīs of the north.

One should give a strip of buffalo-hide to the yoginīs of the northeast, a strip of donkey-hide to the yoginīs of the northwest, a strip of jackal-hide to the yoginīs of the southwest, and a strip of camel-hide to the yoginīs of the southeast.

Having given the *tālikā* [signal], he should then give a skull-cup— whether in one piece, two pieces, or three pieces, as it may be obtained— of the deceased from his own family to the yoginīs for the purpose of drinking. Then, having placed the solid food in a small plate and the drink in a lotus-vessel, the practitioner should circumambulate [the assembly] three times, worship them with perfumes, flowers, incense, and so forth, and make this request:
Then one should dedicate [the merit]:
"By this merit, may all sentient beings become attainers of the knowledge of Mahāmudrā.
This *gaṇacakra* should be performed by the king.
Through common [means], by the power of mantra, or by the restriction of the deity, otherwise there would be a flaw for practitioners.

The communal feast (*gaṇacakra*) should be performed according to the customs of one's region and family; it should be carried out at home by noble women who have been properly prepared for the sake of accumulating merit.
Otherwise, it is not a *gaṇacakra*.

Devoid of the bliss of wisdom and means (*prajñopāya*), and lacking the tasting of the bodhicitta through sexual union, it is called merely a "hero's meal" (*vīrabhojana*) consisting of food and drink alone, not a *gaṇacakra*.
That very [service] should be performed by lay practitioners (upāsakas), with the preceptor (ācārya) as the principal figure.

Furthermore, in the Mantra system, the preceptor is of three kinds—the householder, the celibate student (cellaka), and the monk—corresponding respectively to the inferior, middling, and superior [levels].
Thus,
even if a householder has full knowledge of the ten principles (*daśatattva*), he is not equal to one who has been consecrated and authorized,
because of the words spoken by the Blessed One in the Tantra.

At the time of exposition, even though both of them— the householder and the renunciant— are under the authority of the guru, the monks who observe the vows must perform prostrations to them, honoring the True Dharma and so forth, but not at any other time when there is no exposition. At other times, when they have arrived as guests, one should show all respect, such as by offering them seats and the like.
"Having abandoned improper ritual worship" means:

having abandoned improper acts such as washing the feet and so forth, and having abandoned physical, verbal, and mental worship, monks must perform reverence toward the wealth and other possessions of both householders and novices (*cellaka*). Furthermore, for a monk who has previously been consecrated by a Vajrācārya and thus made a Holder of the Vajra (*vajradhara*), it is the rule that monks must perform worship at all times toward that Guru.
Even for a householder and a cellaka who have attained higher realization (*abhijñā*), monks and even the lord of men must perform prostrations to them.
Therefore, there is no confusion among consecrated householders, cellakas, and monks regarding their status as elder or junior, based on the characteristics of seniority.
In this context, between two householders, the one consecrated earlier is the elder.
Likewise among two novices (*cellaka*),
and similarly between two monks (*bhikṣu*), the one who was consecrated first is the elder by virtue of his prior position;

just as the son of a universal monarch (*cakravartin*) becomes a universal monarch when consecrated, the son of a king becomes a king when consecrated, and the son of a minister becomes a minister when consecrated.

Likewise, the consecrated monk becomes the principal preceptor (pradhānācārya), the novice (cellaka) becomes the intermediate preceptor (madhyamācārya), and the householder becomes the lowest preceptor (adhamācārya). Therefore, among these three, the monk comes first and Vajradhara [the householder] second; he is made the leader of the assembly (gaṇanāyaka) in the feast circle (gaṇacakra), the consecration ceremony (pratiṣṭhā), and so forth. In his absence, the novice [takes his place], and in his absence as well, the householder.
When a monk who is an *ācārya* is not made the leader of the community by the donor, even though he is available, then through the transgression of failing to honor those worthy of honor,

there occurs for the donors a reversal of merit due to the defilement of the saffron-colored mark (*kāṣāyaliṅga*). Therefore, one endowed with all virtues, who bears the banner of the Omniscient One and has abandoned the ten unwholesome paths of action,
should be appointed as the leader of the community.
One who is pitiless, wrathful, cruel, stubborn, greedy, and unrestrained—
who exalts himself— should not be made [a recipient] by a donor seeking the bliss of a Buddha.
